Pay particular attention to branch points, reconverging paths, wire crossings, and inversion bubbles. Treat two crossing wires as connected only when an explicit junction is present. Do not infer connectivity from visual alignment or proximity. Distinguish the gate types from their symbols, particularly OR and XOR gates, and account for every inversion bubble. Once the connectivity has been established, propagate the Boolean signals through the gates and simplify the resulting expression for (Q). Return only the final fully simplified Boolean expression for (Q).
img_desc:
A schematic diagram illustrating a multi-level combinational logic circuit composed of 10 standard digital logic gates driven by three independent primary input lines on the left, labeled A, B, and C, and producing a single primary output labeled Q on the far right.

The three primary inputs run horizontally across the schematic from left to right as reference rails: rail A along the top, rail B through the middle, and rail C along the bottom. Explicit solid circular junction dots designate galvanic connections where signal branches diverge from the primary rails, whereas perpendicular wire crossings without dots represent electrically non-connecting crossovers.

The circuit contains 10 logic gates categorized by standard IEEE/ANSI distinct-shape symbols:

Gate 1 (Top-Left XOR): A 2-input XOR gate positioned in the upper-left quadrant. Its upper input taps directly from rail A, and its lower input connects via an explicit junction dot to rail B.
Gate 2 (Middle-Left OR): A 2-input OR gate situated below Gate 1. Its upper input connects via a vertical wire tapping rail A at an explicit junction dot, and its lower input connects to rail B.
Gate 3 (Lower-Left Inverter): A single-input NOT gate (triangle with an inversion bubble) positioned below rail B. Its input taps a branch from rail B, producing an inverted signal.
Gate 4 (Upper-Middle AND): A 2-input AND gate located in the upper-middle section. Its upper input connects to the output of Gate 1, and its lower input taps rail C through an explicit junction dot.
Gate 5 (Center XOR): A 2-input XOR gate situated immediately downstream of Gate 2. Its upper input connects to rail B, and its lower input receives the output of Gate 2.
Gate 6 (Center-Right AND): A 2-input AND gate receiving the output of Gate 4 on its upper input and the output of Gate 5 on its lower input.
Gate 7 (Bottom NAND): A 2-input NAND gate (flat input back with two distinct inputs and an inversion bubble at the output) located in the lower-middle region. Its upper input receives the branch from the Inverter, and its lower input receives a branch tapping rail C at a junction dot.
Gate 8 (Reconvergent XOR): A 2-input XOR gate combining the output of Gate 6 on its upper input and the output of Gate 7 on its lower input.
Gate 9 (Top-Right NOR): A 2-input NOR gate (curved input back with an inversion bubble at the output) positioned in the upper-right section. Its upper input connects to rail A via a vertical branch with an explicit junction dot, and its lower input receives the output of Gate 8.
Gate 10 (Output XOR): A 2-input XOR gate at the final output stage. Its upper input receives the output of Gate 9, and its lower input connects via a vertical branch tapping rail C at an explicit junction dot, producing primary output Q.
